title: Projective complete linear systems on a Borel quotient
statement: Let $F$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure]. Group schemes and their homomorphisms are as in [def-sc-group-scheme]. All algebraic groups in this statement are affine and of finite type over $F$ [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Smoothness and connectedness are as in [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-connected-scheme]. A Borel subgroup of a smooth connected group $G$ is a maximal smooth connected solvable closed subgroup; solvable means that iterating the derived subgroup eventually gives the trivial group, and the derived subgroup is the smallest closed subgroup through which the commutator morphism factors. Let $G$ be smooth connected and $B\subseteq G$ a Borel subgroup. The quotient $Q=G/B$ means the $F$-scheme representing the fppf sheafification of $A\mapsto G(A)/B(A)$ on commutative $F$-algebras; here fppf coverings are jointly surjective faithfully flat finitely presented coverings. Write $\pi:G\to Q$ for the quotient morphism. Let $\mathcal L$ be an invertible $\mathcal O_Q$-module (Zariski locally isomorphic to $\mathcal O_Q$), with $V=\Gamma(Q,\mathcal L)\ne0$. For a nonzero finite-dimensional $F$-vector space $V$, $\mathbf P(V)$ is the scheme of one-dimensional quotients of $V$, with tautological quotient line bundle $\mathcal O_{\mathbf P(V)}(1)$; $\operatorname{GL}(V)$ is the group scheme $A\mapsto\operatorname{Aut}_A(V\otimes_F A)$, $\operatorname{SL}(V)$ is its determinant-one subgroup, and $\operatorname{PGL}(V)$ is the fppf sheaf quotient of $\operatorname{GL}(V)$ by its scalar subgroup $\mathbf G_m$, where $\mathbf G_m(A)=A^\times$ [def-sc-gm-ga]. Then $V$ is finite-dimensional, evaluation $V\otimes_F\mathcal O_Q\to\mathcal L$ is surjective, and there is a group-scheme homomorphism $a:G\to\operatorname{PGL}(V)$ for which its evaluation morphism $t:Q\to\mathbf P(V)$ is equivariant for left translation of $G$ on $Q$, and $t^*\mathcal O_{\mathbf P(V)}(1)\simeq\mathcal L$. The tautological line has its natural $\operatorname{GL}(V)$-linearization: an algebraic left action on its total space, linear on fibres and covering the projective action, satisfying the group action identities. All equivariance assertions are identities of scheme morphisms, hence hold after every commutative $F$-algebra extension.

source.place: Proposition 18.22, proof, printed p.393, paragraph beginning Let V, and 18.12--18.13, printed p.390: projective complete-linear-system maps and the homogeneous tautological line (Iversen 1976, 1.2--1.3).

proof.text: By [lem-sfb-homogeneous-orbit-quotient-geometry], the represented quotient $Q$ is separated and of finite type over $F$. By [lem-sfb-borel-characteristic-picard-sequence], $\pi$ is a Zariski locally trivial $B$-torsor. Its local product description makes it of finite presentation (on a trivializing open it is projection from the finite-type $F$-group $B$), and gives the ratio and local-lifting conditions of [lem-sfb-borel-quotient-proper-geometry]. That node therefore makes $G$ and $Q$ smooth geometrically integral, and $Q$ proper and Noetherian. By [lem-sfb-borel-quotient-affine-space-cell], $Q$ has a dense affine-space open. An invertible sheaf is quasi-coherent and finitely presented: on each trivializing open it is the free module of rank one. Thus [lem-fin-proper-coherent-finite-dimensional], in degree zero, gives $\dim_F V<\infty$. By [lem-pc-h0-proper-variety], $\Gamma(Q,\mathcal O_Q)=F$.

source.place: Proposition 18.22, printed p.393, construction of f and t; expanded using the cited generic inputs.

proof.text: Write $c:Q\times_FG\to Q$, $c(x,g)=g^{-1}x$. Apply [lem-sfb-affine-cell-picard-product] to $X=Q$, $T=G$, $t_0=e$ and $H=c^*\mathcal L$. Its hypotheses hold by step 1, and $H_e=\mathcal L$ by the action identity. We obtain a line bundle $N$ on $G$ and an isomorphism $c^*\mathcal L\cong p_Q^*\mathcal L\otimes p_G^*N$. Trivialize $N$ on an affine open cover $G_i=\operatorname{Spec}A_i$ of $G$. This gives isomorphisms $\phi_i:c^*\mathcal L\to p_Q^*\mathcal L$ on $Q\times G_i$; on each overlap their ratio is multiplication by a unit pulled back from the overlap. In particular every translation by an element of $G(F)$ preserves the isomorphism class of $\mathcal L$.

source.place: Proposition 18.22, printed p.393, construction of f and t; expanded using the cited generic inputs.

proof.text: Choose $0\ne s\in V$. It is nonvanishing on a nonempty open of $Q$: on a trivializing open a nonzero local representative is a nonzero regular function on the integral scheme $Q$, so its principal open is nonempty. By [lem-sc-lft-over-field-jacobson-space] and [lem-weil-pbc-closed-point-residue-field-base] this open has a point $y\in Q(F)$. By [lem-sfb-homogeneous-orbit-quotient-geometry], $Q(F)=G(F)/B(F)$; hence for every $x\in Q(F)$ there is $g\in G(F)$ with $g^{-1}x=y$. The isomorphism in step 2 sends the inverse-translate of $s$ to a global section nonzero at $x$. Thus the evaluation map is surjective at every closed point. In a local trivialization its cokernel is $\mathcal O_Q/(s_1,\ldots,s_r)$ for a basis of $V$; its support is closed. If that support were nonempty it would contain a closed point by the same Jacobson node, a contradiction. Evaluation is therefore surjective everywhere.

source.place: Proposition 18.22, printed p.393, construction of f and t; expanded using the cited generic inputs.

proof.text: The quotient classification [lem-trf-projective-bundle-quotient-geometry], for $S=\operatorname{Spec}F$ and the quasi-coherent module associated to $V$, now turns evaluation into $t:Q\to\mathbf P(V)$ with a quotient-compatible isomorphism $t^*\mathcal O(1)\cong\mathcal L$. We use exactly its convention $\mathbf P(V)=\operatorname{Proj}(\operatorname{Sym}V)$, classifying rank-one quotients, rather than the convention of lines in $V$.

source.place: Proposition 18.22, printed p.393, construction of f and t; expanded using the cited generic inputs.

proof.text:
By [lem-pc-flat-base-change-cohom] in degree zero, for every $F$-algebra $A$ the pullback map identifies $\Gamma(Q_A,\mathcal L_A)$ with $V\otimes_FA$, naturally in $A$. On $G_i$, compose inverse-translation pullback with $\phi_i$ to obtain an invertible $A_i$-linear operator
$$R_i(g)s(x)=\phi_{i,(x,g)}\bigl(s(g^{-1}x)\bigr).$$
Invertibility follows by applying the inverse isomorphism of line bundles and the inverse of the automorphism $(x,g)\mapsto(g^{-1}x,g)$ of $Q\times G_i$ over $G_i$. Choose an $F$-basis of $V$. The matrix entries of $R_i$ and its inverse belong to $A_i$, so $R_i:G_i\to\operatorname{GL}(V)$ is a scheme morphism. On overlaps the operators differ by the scalar transition unit of $N$. Their images therefore glue in the quotient sheaf $\operatorname{GL}(V)/\mathbf G_m=\operatorname{PGL}(V)$ to a scheme morphism $a:G\to\operatorname{PGL}(V)$, independent of the trivializations.

source.place: Proposition 18.22, printed p.393, construction of f and t; expanded using the cited generic inputs.

proof.text: To check multiplication, work on affine opens of $G\times G$ where the line $N$ is trivial on both factors and after multiplication. Both $R(g)R(h)$ and $R(gh)$ are obtained from isomorphisms from $\mathcal L_{h^{-1}g^{-1}x}$ to $\mathcal L_x$, because $h^{-1}g^{-1}=(gh)^{-1}$. Their ratio is an automorphism of an invertible sheaf, hence a unit on $Q\times\operatorname{Spec}A$. By [lem-pc-h0-proper-variety] and [lem-pc-flat-base-change-cohom] applied to $\mathcal O_Q$, this ring is $A$; the ratio is a scalar unit from $A$. Consequently $[R(g)R(h)]=[R(gh)]$ in PGL on these opens, and thus globally. The same calculation at $e$ makes $R(e)$ scalar, so $a(e)=1$. These are identities of scheme morphisms, proving that $a$ is a group-scheme homomorphism. The scalar argument was over the universal parameter opens, so it is valid after arbitrary, including nonreduced, base change.

source.place: Proposition 18.22, printed p.393, construction of f and t; expanded using the cited generic inputs.

proof.text:
The natural left action of $u\in\operatorname{GL}(V)$ on a quotient $q:V_A\twoheadrightarrow M$ sends it to $q\circ u^{-1}$. Quotient functoriality in [lem-trf-projective-bundle-quotient-geometry] makes this an algebraic action, and scalar matrices fix its projective point, so it descends to PGL. On $Q\times G_i$, the defining formula for $R_i$ gives
$$\operatorname{ev}_{gx}\circ R_i(g)=\phi_{i,(gx,g)}\circ\operatorname{ev}_x.$$
Thus $\operatorname{ev}_{gx}$ and $\operatorname{ev}_x\circ R_i(g)^{-1}$ are isomorphic quotient pairs. The quotient classification identifies their morphisms: $t(gx)=a(g)t(x)$. This is an identity over $G_i\times Q$, and hence over $G\times Q$ after gluing. Its pullback gives the asserted equivariance for every $F$-algebra.

source.place: Proposition 18.22, printed p.393, construction of f and t; expanded using the cited generic inputs.

proof.text: Finally the same quotient functor supplies the tautological $\operatorname{GL}(V)$-linearization: over a point $q:V_A\twoheadrightarrow M$, send the fibre $M$ linearly by the identity to the fibre presented by $q\circ u^{-1}:V_A\twoheadrightarrow M$. This rule respects isomorphisms of quotient pairs and arbitrary pullbacks, so [lem-trf-projective-bundle-quotient-geometry] makes it an algebraic isomorphism between the two pulled-back tautological lines on $\operatorname{GL}(V)\times\mathbf P(V)$. The formula for two successive operations is $q\circ v^{-1}\circ u^{-1}=q\circ(uv)^{-1}$; identity matrices give the identity. These equalities also hold on the fibres, proving the action and cocycle identities. Thus the induced action on the total line is algebraic and linear on fibres, as in Milne 18.12--18.13.
